name: Calcium ruthenate
equilibrium_context: Orbital-selective Mott insulator (S=1), insulator-metal transition at about 357 K in the bulk, shifted in strained thin films

driven_states.emergent_property: Optical excitation first leads to a fast lattice rearrangement (volume expansion), and only afterwards does the electronic transition into a metastable non-equilibrium state follow. Unusual: the lattice leads, not the electrons.
driven_states.source: Verma, Gorobtsov, ..., Singer, Nature Physics 20, 807 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41567-024-02396-1
further_sources: Suen et al., Nature Physics 20, 1757 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41567-024-02629-3 (current-induced IMT: the driven phase is electronically distinct from the thermal high-T metallic phase)
Nakamura et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 2536 (2013), doi:10.1038/srep02536
driven_states.caveat: The paper does not classify the transition as purely electronic - on the contrary, its central claim is that a volume expansion precedes the electronic transition. On the other hand, Suen et al. show for the current-driven case that the non-equilibrium state is not identical to the thermal metal, and hence not purely thermal either. Both statements come from one group each.

gaps: Fluence threshold and exact lifetime not verified against the full text.
